title: One note after another
summary: Hear an ordered group of notes.

steps.title: One note after another
steps.body:
**scale** means a group of notes played in order, going higher or lower. Play one note, let it go, then play the next. Today use C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C. The last C is one octave above the first.

**Why it matters:** A scale gives you a small set of sounds to learn instead of guessing across the whole guitar.

steps.title: Find the notes
steps.body: Start on string 5, fret 3 for C3. Take your time: the check follows note names in order, without a speed target.

items.prompt: Play C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C in that order, one note at a time.

steps.title: Make it familiar
steps.body: Play the first three notes C, D, E slowly. Then find another place for C3; moving to another string does not change the sound.

items.prompt: Play C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C in that order, one note at a time.
